text: Other essential items were purchased throughout Q5 and Q6. Milestone 5.2: Test and/or Design Equipment This milestone represented the placement of testing and/or design equipment for the office and lab spaces, including computers, server for data storage and wind tunnel instrumentation. The spaces were considered ready for experimental and scientific operation. Deliverable 5.2 Test and/or Design Equipment Equipment was ordered and received throughout the project. Long lead-time items were processed with purchase orders early in the project during Q2 and Q3 and short lead-time items began processing in Q4. Installation into the renovated space was completed throughout Q4 - Q6. By the end of the project, the final list of items was purchased and received with two exceptions. An industrial 3D printer and a lab table were delayed due to supply chain disruptions and tariff adjustments. These items were received and installed shortly after the end of Q6. Issues, Risks, and Mitigation At the end of the first quarter, funding was released to UTD in November 2023. Through the University financial process, a cost center was generated to deposit the funds for usage throughout the project. This cost center was established in December. With the funds in place, our Facilities Management team solicited three official bids from General Contractors. The University went on winter break which caused delay. By the end of January 2024, a General Contractor was selected, and work was scheduled to begin at the start of Q2. The General Contractor generated a schedule to mitigate time loss to reach the planned tasks and milestones by the end of Q4. The project proceeded according to the revised schedule and experienced a few delays in Q4. As a result, a 6-month co-cost extension was requested and granted for the following reasons: • Fiscal year rollover (FY 24 to FY 25) caused delay in purchasing o UTD FY24 ended August 31st with final close of purchasing on August 23rd o UTD eProcurement was offline August 28th – September 5th • Construction delay in support for wind/wave tunnel o Contractors (included in current contractual support) delayed finishing renovation until after wind/wave tunnel was installed. The installation took several weeks past the initial projected deadline due to several factors such as delays from the manufacturer to ship the pieces of the equipment, equipment failure during calibration and testing, and plumbing redesign based on the failure during testing. Changes to Scope, Schedule, Budget, or Team The scope of work and team remained unchanged throughout the project. The schedule was adjusted to complete tasks 1-4 during Q2 and Q3 and the General Contractor agreed to work within our scheduled parameters. Tasks 1-3 were completed by Q3, and Task 4 was completed shortly after the start of Q4 after the installation of access controls. The schedule was then re-adjusted as a result of the no-cost extension granted by DOE. Task 5 was completed by the end of Q6 and receipt of all remaining equipment occurred in the weeks following the close of Q6.
